cohorts.subjects: Rows whose source_of_values is 'this paper'. Living adult patients with multislice CT of the lumbosacral spine for pain in the lumbar spine, referred by specialists in various fields, at the Radiology Department of the General Hospital 'Prim. Dr. Abdulah Nakas', Sarajevo, Bosnia and Herzegovina, scanned 1 January 2013 to 31 December 2014; retrospective. Ethnicity printed only as the population of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Excluded: congenital and acquired spinal deformities, benign and malignant changes of the spine, traumatic, inflammatory and pronounced degenerative changes; how many were screened is not given. Every patient carries one of four disc diagnoses made at the CT reading (bulged disc, herniation, protrusion, extrusion; Table 2). The 'not stated' rows of this source are the P-values of Tables 6-11, which compare these patients with other studies.
cohorts.n_units: 1,000 lumbar levels (L1 to L5) of 200 patients, each level with one midsagittal and one interpedicular diameter; Table 5 prints n = 100 per sex, level and measure
cohorts.ages: men mean 43.84 (text 43.8), SD 10.99, range 20-60 years; women mean 43.78, SD 6.00, range 27-50 years (Table 1 and text)

techniques.instrument: 40-slice CT, Siemens Somatom Definition AS; 120 kV, 266 mAs, acquisition 40 x 0.6 mm, 2 mm layers; axial scans with coronal and sagittal multiplanar reconstructions from T12 to S1; bone window 2300-2500 HU and soft-tissue window 300-500 HU; measured on screen with Siemens Syngo software in the bone window
techniques.how: Both diameters in the axial plane, with the reconstructions linking axial, coronal and sagittal views. Midsagittal diameter (MSG, MSGD; MSAG in Figure 1): along the midline, from the back edge of the vertebral body to the front (inner) edge of the lamina where the spinous process separates from the arch; the same sentence also says it was measured in the midsagittal plane. Interpedicular diameter (IP, IPD; 'interpeduncular' in the abstract): at the canal's widest point, the transverse distance between the inner edges of the two pedicles. Figure 1 draws both lines on one axial slice through the pedicles; which slice per vertebra, and whether the plane was angled to the vertebra, is not stated. Levels L1 to L5; how the levels were counted is not stated. Ranges read to 0.1 mm.

within_paper: One cohort of 200 patients. The midsagittal and interpedicular diameters were both measured on each patient's same CT, L1 to L5 (p. 201, PDF 2), so the two measures share every subject. Tables 3, 4 and 5 are the same measurements: Tables 3 and 4 print Table 5's four-decimal means cut to two decimals, with two disagreements, women's L3 midsagittal minimum (12.20 in Table 3, 13.50 in Table 5) and women's L4 midsagittal mean (17.38 in Table 3, 17.1420 in Table 5) (p. 202, PDF 3); Inference: the Table 3 figures are the misprints, since the both-sexes minimum 12.30 and mean 16.79 fit Table 5. The 'Our study' columns of Tables 6 to 11 repeat Tables 3 and 4 (pp. 203-204, PDF 4-5), and Table 2 and Chart 1 give the CT diagnoses of the same 200 (p. 201, PDF 2). The comparator cohorts are separate studies; the paper states no overlap between them and its own patients.
